message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to two very different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their last common ancestor is therefore not a specific “species” but a more primitive placental mammal that lived roughly 100 million years ago during the late Cretaceous. This ancestor would have been a small, shrew‑like mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
